name: Impressionism
summary: Painting of the first look: quick, broken strokes of pure colour that record changing light on a modern scene. The painters work outdoors, drop the outline and the black shadow, and let the viewer's eye mix the colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture records the impression of light on a surface at one moment, not the object as it is known to be.
design_principles: Paint the scene in one session of 2 hours or less, so that the light is the same across the canvas.
Apply colour in separate, visible touches of 5–20mm and let them mix in the eye at a distance.
Paint shadow in colour: use blue, violet or green at the same value as the lit ground, and use no black.
Set the value range narrow: most of the picture sits within 3 or 4 steps of a 10-step scale.
Put complementary pairs side by side (orange and blue, red and green) to make the vibration of light.
Crop as a snapshot: let the edge cut figures and objects, and place the horizon high or low.
Choose modern leisure as the subject: boulevards, rivers, gardens, stations and cafés.
anti_patterns: Black outlines or hard contours around forms
Dark, low-key ground and a single dramatic beam of light
Detailed, sharp rendering of faces and leaves

composition.layout: An open, snapshot-like frame with an uneven weight; diagonal paths, rivers and rows of trees lead the eye, and there is no central pyramid.
composition.focal_point: A small area of the strongest contrast or the warmest colour, on a third line, at 15–25% of the picture area.
composition.format: Landscape canvas at 4:3 or 3:2; figures and objects are cropped by the edges; the horizon sits at 1/3 or 2/3.

principles.rule: Place the horizon at 1/3 or 2/3 of the height, and the main accent near a third intersection.
Let sky, water or a wall of bright light fill 30–50% of the canvas.
Use a road, a river bank or a row of trees as a diagonal that enters from a corner.
Set 60% of the area in a dominant key (all warm or all cool), 30% in its neighbours, and 10% in the complement.
Use an edge crop or a foreground branch to frame the view, as if the painter had no time to arrange it.

palette.strategy: A bright, high-key palette of pure pigments, with shadows in complementary colour and a few mixed greys; the colour is optical, and mixing stays on the canvas.
palette.distribution: Light and mid values 70–80%, saturated touches 15–20%, dark accents under 10%.
palette.ground: A pale, light-grey or cream commercial ground, which shows through gaps between touches.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint from pre-made metal tubes, applied wet-in-wet.
brushwork_and_medium.support: A portable canvas, 50 by 65cm or smaller, with a pale commercial ground.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Short, broken strokes of 5–20mm, laid in different directions for each element: horizontal for water, vertical for trees, a dab for flowers.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: Alla prima in one session; thick paint (impasto) in the lights and thin, dragged paint in the shadows; colours stay unmixed on the palette.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Lost or vibrating edges: a form dissolves into its neighbour; no outline anywhere.

light_and_modelling.light: Natural daylight outdoors, which changes with the hour; the picture shows one hour and one weather.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Form is built by a change of colour temperature and not by dark and light: a warm lit side against a cool shadow side at the same value.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Coloured shadow in blue or violet with a value only 1–2 steps below the light; reflected colour from nearby surfaces.
light_and_modelling.temperature: A dominant warm light against cool shadow, or the reverse at dusk; the contrast is the picture.

subject.typical: Gardens, rivers and bridges, haystacks, boulevards in rain, cafés and railway stations, promenading figures.
subject.figure_scale: Figures are small and sketched (10–40% of the height), or they are cropped by the edge.
subject.treatment: Faces are suggested by 2–3 touches; modern life as it is, with no moral or myth.

surface.finish: Matt to semi-matt, with no varnish on the first exhibitions.
surface.texture: Strong impasto ridges and a visible weave; the surface looks like fast work.

works.work: Stacks of Wheat (End of Day, Autumn)

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). Look at the museum page for the image and its licence.

positive: coloured shadows in violet and blue

emotion.target_response: Light and ease: the viewer feels a warm day, a passing mood and a pleasure in looking.

avoid_when: The brief needs exact detail: a product, a diagram, a face that must be recognised.
The brief asks for a hard graphic outline or a dark dramatic mood.

modifiers.how: Keep the colour touches; make each one a faceted plane with a straight edge, narrow the palette to 3–4 hues, and drop the atmosphere.
Keep the cropped viewpoint and the high horizon; replace the touches with flat fields and a 1–2mm contour.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
John Rewald, The History of Impressionism (MoMA, 1946)
